sections.title: What this was
sections.body:
You were given one URL and three emails. Within a few hours that grew into an operation of fourteen personas and nine domains, assembled inside one quarter and switched on three months before the first contact with the client.

But the point of this case is not the size of the find — it is the level you stopped at. Below it lies 'just a bad recruiter', above it 'state intelligence'. Both look convincing and both cost the client dearly: the first leads her to answer the questionnaire, the second to make a claim she cannot support.

sections.title: The correct pivot chain
sections.body:
Step 1. Do not open with image search. The move is obvious, cheap, and in a case about a generated persona it adds nothing: zero matches is exactly what any synthetic face returns.

Step 2. Start with what can be checked. The synthetic detector gives a positive signal, the domain gives a registration date, the headers give a route. Three checkable things against one uncheckable one.

Step 3. Expand from the domain to the block. One suspicious domain is an observation. Nine domains in one quarter on one block with one MX is a purchase, and a purchase had a budget.

Step 4. Expand from domains to people. A domain farm proves intent but not activity. Sweeping LinkedIn across the eight names turns inventory into an operation.

Step 5. Read the questionnaire as a document, not as a conversation. Twelve questions say a great deal through their content and more through their absences: nothing about money, terms or procurement.

sections.title: Three axes, and why exactly three
sections.body:
Technical axis: synthetic faces, a closed endorsement ring, an identical gap between registration and first activity. Infrastructural: a shared hosting block, a shared MX, the same commercial template, one registration quarter. Behavioural: fourteen personas running one scenario, a 17%-against-78% question split, a missing hiring frame.

Each one alone has an answer waiting. Synthetic faces? Detectors get it wrong. Shared hosting? Cheap provider, everyone is there. Strange questions? Clumsy recruiters exist. Together those answers stop working: to keep the innocent explanation you would have to assume three independent coincidences at once.

And separately, about what did not make it into those axes. Five reverse searches that found nothing are not five pieces of evidence and not even one: they all look into the same indexed web, and a generated face has nothing to match. Being able to subtract a correlated signal from your own list of supports is worth more than being able to add one.

sections.title: The ladder, rung by rung
sections.body:
Identifier. There is no name here and there will not be one: an operation stands behind the persona. That is not a failure of the investigation, it is its result. The weaker card 'Sonia is fake' disqualifies the persona without naming the actor; the card 'Sonia, Principal Talent Partner' merely retells the profile the persona wrote about itself.

Location is this case's inversion. The answer that looks most precise scores zero: Amsterdam and Frankfurt are a property of a data centre, and Moldova on the route looks sinister exactly in proportion to how cheap it is. Full credit goes to a documented boundary of knowledge plus the weak thing genuinely obtained: the working hours point at GMT+3. That narrows without naming — and that is how it should be written down.

Motive. It rests on three axes, two of which are about absences. No questions about money or terms, nothing that would sell on the candidate-data market. Absence proves more here than presence: the content of a conversation can be faked, its purpose cannot.

Timeline. The order matters more than the dates: domains first, then personas, then the target. An opportunist runs the sequence backwards — sees the target first, then improvises.

Verification. The methodological rung: it adds no facts, it shows why the other four hold.

sections.title: 'So what?' — why the third option
sections.body:
The CV scam does not add up against the costs: data trading lives on volume, and here we have nine domains and three months of preparation for one company.

The bad agency does not add up against the deliberateness: incompetence explains clumsy questions, but not twelve synthetic faces and an endorsement ring. That does not happen by accident.

State intelligence does not add up against the budget. Every individual argument for it is true: the sector is strategic, the competitor at a state institute exists, precedents for the scheme are documented. But no tool showed a link between those facts and this cluster, and the infrastructure argues the other way: an off-the-shelf template, a $49 mailer, card-rented VPS. A state fingerprint is recognized by what the infrastructure cost, not by how sinister the jurisdiction looks.

The third option remains. A commercial technology-acquisition operation, attributed to the operation rather than to a person.

sections.title: What to carry into the next case
sections.body:
Rule one. The level of the claim cannot exceed the level of the evidence. Overreach destroys a case not when it is made but when the case has to be defended: one contradictory fact takes down everything, including the part that was true.

Rule two. Absence of proof is not proof of absence. An empty search result argues neither way; what argues is the tool that returns a positive signal.

Rule three. Axes count by independence, not by number. Five looks into one index is one look. Before counting your supports, check whether they come from the same source.

Rule four. Look at what is not there. The missing hiring frame in correspondence about hiring said more in this case than any individual questionnaire item.

sections.title: Tools
sections.body:
LinkedIn Sales Navigator — paid, gives deep profile analysis without notifying the target. For persona work in 2026 this is baseline equipment, not a luxury.

Sensity.ai — a standalone synthetic-face detector, free tier gives a few checks a day. It is that rare tool which returns a positive signal where everything else returns emptiness.

FaceCheck.id and PimEyes — reverse face search. They find reuse of real photographs. Their indexes overlap substantially, so they cannot be counted as two independent sources.

ViewDNS.info and DomainTools — reverse WHOIS and reverse IP. These are what turn one domain into a block.

Wayback Machine — snapshot history. A site that has not changed in nine months says more about a company than its About page does.

Full email headers — the Received chain, Return-Path, DKIM. Free, always available, and regularly worth more than every paid subscription combined.

sections.title: Boundaries and ethics
sections.body:
Do not write to the target. The question 'are you a real person?' costs you not reputation but the case: the cluster gets the signal and folds, taking with it the evidence you had not yet preserved. Passive observation here is not caution, it is the only mode in which evidence survives to the report.

Do not seize the target's infrastructure. Registering a cluster domain 'just to see' moves you out of the observer role and makes what you have collected unusable at exactly the moment it matters.

Do not advise the client to act. Answering the questionnaire with invented data is an operation in which the client carries the risk, and it puts a knowingly false document over their signature into the case file.

Preserve the evidence chain. Raw emails with full headers, timestamped profile captures, saved WHOIS output. Profiles disappear within a day of the first careless move.

Phrase carefully. An accusation of state espionage without proof is not only a methodological error but a legal exposure for the client.

sections.title: Де це розійшлося
sections.body:
Кластер у цій справі знаходять майже всі. Розходиться не на пошуку, а на двох питаннях: до кого саме відноситься атрибуція і на якому рівні її треба зупинити.

Подивись на свою драбину і на відповідь у фіналі — розрив майже напевно там. Далі у цьому розборі те, що мало статися на кожному щаблі, і чому саме так.

Перша — зупинка на «Sonia не існує». Це правда, це доведено, і цього мало: дискваліфікація персони каже, кого немає, і не каже, хто є. Клієнтці від висновку «рекрутерка фальшива» не легшає — питання було, хто за нею стоїть і чого хоче. Відповідь лежала на один крок далі: вісім сусідніх доменів як місце роботи, чотирнадцять профілів, один сценарій.

Друга — стрибок до державної розвідки. Спокуса тут сильна, бо кожен окремий аргумент правдивий: сектор стратегічний, конкурент при державному інституті існує, прецеденти схеми задокументовані. sections.body:
Ідентифікатор. Імені тут немає і не буде: за персоною стоїть операція. Це не поразка розслідування — це його результат. Слабший варіант «Sonia — фальшивка» дискваліфікує персону, але не називає актора; варіант «Sonia, Principal Talent Partner» просто переказує анкету, яку персона написала про себе сама.

Мотив. Тримається на трьох осях, і дві з них — про відсутності. Немає питань про гроші й умови, немає нічого, що продавалося б на ринку кандидатських даних. Відсутність доводить тут більше за присутність: зміст розмови можна підробити, її призначення — ні.

Хронологія. Порядок важить більше за дати: спершу домени, потім персони, потім ціль. Опортуніст ходить у зворотному порядку — спершу бачить ціль, потім імпровізує.

Верифікація. Методологічний щабель: він не додає фактів, він показує, чому попередні чотири тримаються.

sections.body:
Шахрайство на резюме не сходиться з витратами: торгівля даними живе з обсягу, а тут дев'ять доменів і три місяці підготовки заради однієї компанії.

Погана агенція не сходиться з навмисністю: некомпетентність пояснює незграбні питання, але не пояснює дванадцять синтетичних облич і коло схвалень. Так не виходить випадково.

Лишається третій. Комерційна операція зі здобуття технології, атрибутована до операції, а не до особи.

State intelligence does not add up against the budget. Every individual argument for it is true: the sector is strategic, the competitor at a state institute exists, precedents for the scheme are documented. But no tool showed a link between those facts and this cluster, and the infrastructure argues the other way: an off-the-shelf template, a $49 mailer, card-rented VPS. A state fingerprint is recognized by what the infrastructure cost, not by how sinister the jurisdiction looks.

The third option remains. A commercial technology-acquisition operation, attributed to the operation rather than to a person.

sections.title: What to carry into the next case
sections.body:
Rule one. The level of the claim cannot exceed the level of the evidence. Overreach destroys a case not when it is made but when the case has to be defended: one contradictory fact takes down everything, including the part that was true.

Rule two. Absence of proof is not proof of absence. An empty search result argues neither way; what argues is the tool that returns a positive signal.

Rule three. Axes count by independence, not by number. Five looks into one index is one look. Before counting your supports, check whether they come from the same source.

Rule four. Look at what is not there. The missing hiring frame in correspondence about hiring said more in this case than any individual questionnaire item.

sections.title: Tools
sections.body:
LinkedIn Sales Navigator — paid, gives deep profile analysis without notifying the target. For persona work in 2026 this is baseline equipment, not a luxury.

Sensity.ai — a standalone synthetic-face detector, free tier gives a few checks a day. It is that rare tool which returns a positive signal where everything else returns emptiness.

FaceCheck.id and PimEyes — reverse face search. They find reuse of real photographs. Their indexes overlap substantially, so they cannot be counted as two independent sources.

ViewDNS.info and DomainTools — reverse WHOIS and reverse IP. These are what turn one domain into a block.

Wayback Machine — snapshot history. A site that has not changed in nine months says more about a company than its About page does.

Full email headers — the Received chain, Return-Path, DKIM. Free, always available, and regularly worth more than every paid subscription combined.

sections.title: Boundaries and ethics
sections.body:
Do not write to the target. The question 'are you a real person?' costs you not reputation but the case: the cluster gets the signal and folds, taking with it the evidence you had not yet preserved. Passive observation here is not caution, it is the only mode in which evidence survives to the report.

Do not seize the target's infrastructure. Registering a cluster domain 'just to see' moves you out of the observer role and makes what you have collected unusable at exactly the moment it matters.

Do not advise the client to act. Answering the questionnaire with invented data is an operation in which the client carries the risk, and it puts a knowingly false document over their signature into the case file.

Preserve the evidence chain. Raw emails with full headers, timestamped profile captures, saved WHOIS output. Profiles disappear within a day of the first careless move.

Phrase carefully. An accusation of state espionage without proof is not only a methodological error but a legal exposure for the client.
